subject: INLA BYM model prior distribution definition.

messages.author: f7d3b07b7f2eaa84
messages.subject: INLA BYM model prior distribution definition.
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to estimate relative risk using the BYM model, where:
  • r_i: relative risk
  • y_i: observed cases
  • c_i: expected number of cases
And we assume that
  • y_i |r_i ∼ Poisson(c_i * exp{r_i})
  • r_i = Xβ+u_i +v_i.
where
  • u_i : spatial variability
  • v_i : non estructured variability
  • X : covariables matrix
  • β :  regression coefficients vector
and
  • β ∼ N(0,100)
  • π(u) ∝ exp{-SUM [w_ij  φ(u_i - u_j)]}
  • v ∼ N(0,100)
In order to run the model in R, I'm using the following formula:
formula <- round(yi) ~ 1 + cov1 + cov2 + cov3 + cov4 +
                         f(location, model = "bym", graph = poly2nb(map), scale.model = TRUE)

inla_model <- inla(formula, family = "poisson", data = data,
                   control.predictor = list(compute=T, link=1), 
                   E = ci, control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, waic = TRUE))

So, the question is: how can I change the prior beta parameters in the code, for example if I suppose a  N(-5,4) for the regression coefficients, ie, β ∼ N(-5,4).

Thank you.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA BYM model prior distribution definition.
parts:
Hi,

you can change the prior for the regression cooefs, see ?control.fixed,

with

y ~ 1 + x

you can say

control.fixed=list(mean=list(x=1), prec=list(x=2))

meaning beta for x has N() prior with mean 1 and precision 2, just add
more if you have more

control.fixed=list(mean=list(x=1,xx=2), prec=list(x=2,xx=3))


alternative, is the "linear" model, see

inla.doc("linear")

so you can add

y ~ 1 + f(x, model="linear", mean.linear=1, prec.linear=2)

this is just another interface than 'control.fixed' and do the same.

Best
H
